'''Rita Dorothy Guggenheim Lerner''' (May 7, 1929 – July 16, 1994){{r|hoh}} was an American physicist, librarian, editor, and science communicator who worked for many years at the [[American Institute of Physics]]. With [[George L. Trigg]], she was co-editor of the ''[[Encyclopedia of Physics]]'' (Addison-Wesley, 1981).{{r|eop}}

==Life==
Rita Guggenheim was born in [[New York, New York]], in 1929,{{r|hoh|tlq}} and was a 1945 graduate of [[Fiorello H. LaGuardia High School]].{{r|lghs}} She earned a bachelor's degree from [[Radcliffe College]] in 1949,{{r|tlq}} and was managing editor of the college yearbook.{{r|yearbook}} She went to [[Columbia University]] for graduate study, earning a master's degree in 1951 and (as Rita G. Lerner) completing her Ph.D. in 1956;{{r|tlq}} her dissertation was ''Microwave Studies of Molecular Structure''.{{r|diss}}

She came to the American Institute of Physics in the 1960s, hired as part of a program funded by the [[National Science Foundation]] for the improvement of scientific communication.{{r|havens}}

She died on July 16, 1994, in [[Ardsley, New York]].{{r|hoh}}

==Recognition==
Lerner was named a Fellow of the [[American Association for the Advancement of Science]] in 1986.{{r|aaas}}
